blocks.text: Let's look at this one. Starting from negative four is less than two x minus two, which is less than or equal to six, which of these could be the next line? Choose all that apply.
blocks.display: Starting from −4 < 2x − 2 ≤ 6, which of these could be the next line? Select all that apply.

blocks.text: Negative two is less than two x, which is less than or equal to eight. Yes: two was added to all three parts.
Negative two is less than x minus one, which is less than or equal to three. Yes: all three parts were divided by two.
Negative one is less than x, which is less than or equal to four. Yes: that is two steps in one, add two and then divide by two.
Negative six is less than two x, which is less than or equal to four. No: two was subtracted, but the work has minus two, so two must be added.
Negative two is less than two x, which is less than eight. No: the right symbol changed, but each end keeps its own symbol.

Three lines follow: negative two is less than two x, which is less than or equal to eight; negative two is less than x minus one, which is less than or equal to three; and negative one is less than x, which is less than or equal to four. Each one keeps the same solutions.
